title: The 60-second show-and-tell
summary: Give a 60 second talk about something you made or learned this week.

steps.title: Voice, pause, eye contact
steps.body:
Three rules for this talk. Speak to the back wall, loud enough that someone standing there could hear every word. Pause after the sentence that matters most, and let it sit for a second before you move on. Look at one person per sentence, not at the floor or the ceiling.

The question of the week is: what makes something alive? Think about two examples while you plan your talk: is a robot alive, and is a seed alive. Use your answer to the question as the ending of your talk.

steps.title: Prepare the talk
steps.body: Pick one thing you made or learned this week. The badge counts. Write three lines: what it is, the best part, and one thing you would change. Practise saying it twice with a timer running.
checklist: Ends with your answer to the question of the week

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record the talk. Phone propped up, whole face in frame.
